Figure 4: Real-world tasks. Five long-horizon mobile-manipulation tasks, each learned from a single real demonstration: LUNCHBOX, UTENSIL, DROPTRASH, POUR, and FRIDGE.

Figure 11: Demonstration post-process interface used to annotate contact-rich and navigation segments.

Figure 2: Pipeline overview of WANDA. From a single real demonstration, WANDA reconstructs and generates 3D worlds, rearranges contact-rich robot-object interaction segments into diverse spatial configurations, chains them into new trajectories with whole-body motion planning, applies Corrective State Expansion to increase robot and object state coverage, and produces photo-realistic observations by factorized rendering.

Figure 3: Sampled initial configuration results on reconstructed and generated 3D scenes. Scene and robot meshes are shown in Blender. Red regions indicate the object initial pose sampling regions.
